chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: The Nightingale becomes the Little Cotton Club
summary: Willard reads that Frank Sebastian bought the Nightingale and renamed it; Howard's band stayed and Tin Can Henry returned.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I was looking for something that I saw here a minute ago. Just a minute. Oh -- just a minute.
Okay, you should go with it.

I was reading here in this article that and Mrs. Howard both mentioned the Nightingale, which you this is (inaudible) earlier on the tapes -- the Nightingale Club was sold to Frank Sebastian, who renamed it the Little Cotton Club.
And you had been working at the Nightingale, is that right?
Were you working there when Frank Sebastian bought the club?
And then did you continue to work there when it became the Little Cotton Club?
And -- oh, it says that at this time Tin Can Allen returned to the band, returned to your band.
Tin Can Henry. Oh, excuse me.
Here it says Tin Can Allen, but okay, Tin Can Henry. Okay. He came back to your band.
And Lionel left about then. Is that what --
Yeah. I don't know what Lionel did, but he did something else. He was always into something.
